messages:
erin-cs: @here customer reports a spike of 503s for hosted inference around 14:12 UTC, multiple requests failing during long-context, they saw timeouts and then 503s
alex-oncall: looking now, can you paste the customer request id or example?
erin-cs: request id `req_8a9f2b` — happens on large prompt (~120k tokens) streaming calls, they say it worked earlier today
sam-support: customer reported ~80% of attempts failed, some succeeded after retry, billing impact flagged — they asked for ETA and mitigation ASAP :alarm_clock:
liu-eng: initial logs show upstream runner exit with SIGSEGV then kubelet restart: `container exited with code 139` on pod infer-runner-7c9f
infra-bot: Automated alert: Pod infer-runner-7c9f terminated unexpectedly (OOM? segfault). Node gpu-3 reported GPU-reset 14:11:58 UTC
alex-oncall: can you paste dmesg + docker logs snippet?
liu-eng: paste logs below:
```
[14:11:57] infer_runner: allocation failed: out of memory when allocating 4.2 GiB for KV cache
[14:11:57] infer_runner: CUDA error: out of memory
[14:11:57] infer_runner: segfault at 0x7f8a3abcd ip 0x55a1b2c3 sp 0x7ffd2a3e error 6
[14:11:58] kubelet: container "infer-runner" exited with code 139, restarting
```
maya-ml: model: redwood-7b-quant, non-sharded. Large context + dynamic prefetch seems likely to bump KV usage. We recently merged change to prefetch window = 8192 for large-context optimization.
erin-cs: customer says they hit 503s for a 30 minute window, then it recovered. We routed some traffic to fallback model and they had partial success.
sam-support: reopened billing hold until we confirm no overcount due to retries. CS asked for repro steps and ETA.
liu-eng: repro plan: run load test with sequence length ~120k, batch size 2, prefetch window 8192, run on a single GPU image. Will capture coredump if segfault repeats.
alex-oncall: temporary mitigation: scale down prefetch window to 2048 via runtime flag, enable smaller KV cap, and apply pod anti-affinity to avoid packing this workload. Also enable fallback routing for that customer to redwood-7b-quant-safe variant.
maya-ml: agree — lowering prefetch avoids KV blowout but may increase latency. Recommend canary change for single host first.
erin-cs: I'll notify customer of mitigation and ETA ~45m for canary + monitoring. They want root cause timeline.
liu-eng: follow-ups: 1) capture core + nvcrash logs if it reproduces, 2) check if new prefetch patch changed memory accounting, 3) add safety clamp on KV allocation per request.
alex-oncall: I'm patching runtime flag now — rolling to 5% of runners in staging, then 25%. Will post rollout status.
infra-bot: Rollout: infer-runtime config updated: prefetch_window=2048 -> 5% of pool (started).
liu-eng: added repro script in /internal/triage/1733333333-repro.sh and a short checklist.
sam-support: noted — CS updated customer, put them on watch.
erin-cs: customer appreciated quick mitigation, asked for postmortem and whether retries count to billing.
sam-support: billing will not charge for failed attempts while we investigate — follow-up via invoice team.
alex-oncall: final note: root cause suspected: prefetch-memory regression under large context triggering CUDA OOM followed by segfault; mitigation applied. Will create postmortem and link once ready. :thumbsup:
